problem: Given the polynomial $P(x)=x(x+3)(x-2),$ find the solution of $P(x)<0.$
worked_solution:
To solve the inequality $P(x)<0,$ we need to find the values of $x$ for which the curve $y=P(x)$ lies below the $x$-axis.

The roots of the polynomial $P(x)=x(x+3)(x-2)$ are $x=-3,x=0$ and $x=2,$ which are all simple roots.

Also, $P(x)$ is a cubic polynomial with a positive leading coefficient. So, we can graph the curve as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14033945/assets/d87500612fc14636afa38bd01fdc1b90cf7eecd0bfbd546bff7b14d5a5b30fc8.png)

Since we are interested in solving $P(x)<0,$ we look for the part of the curve that is below the $x$-axis. 

Based on the graph, the solution is $x\in (-\infty ,-3)\cup (0,2).$
